items.description: `parseRedisUrl` called `new URL(url)` with no try/catch, so a malformed `E2E_REDIS_URL` (e.g. `'plain-hostname'`) threw Node's generic `TypeError: Invalid URL` instead of going through the function's own diagnostic path that names the env var and redacts credentials. Operators debugging a bad Redis URL saw an unhelpful stock error rather than the intended guidance.

`parseRedisUrl` lived as a free function inside `global-setup.ts` (a composition root) instead of as a static method on `RedisTestContainer`, unlike the sibling `PostgresTestContainer.isDockerAvailable()` which is a static on its own container class. That placement meant a future change to the parsed connection shape would require edits in two files instead of one.

`QueueModule`'s barrel omitted re-exports for `BULLMQ_PREFIX_TOKEN` and the `BullmqPrefix` type, breaking the project's module convention (already followed by the sibling `BullBoardAuthModule`) of re-exporting DI tokens/types that are part of a module's public surface, forcing cross-module consumers to import from the internal file path directly.

`PostgresTestContainer` and `RedisTestContainer` were started sequentially in `setup()`, with Redis start gated behind Postgres start plus all migrations even though the two container starts are independent — adding roughly 2-4 seconds of unnecessary wall-clock latency to every test run.

The exported `RedisContainerConfig` and `RedisContainerInfo` interfaces carried no JSDoc, even though the sibling `postgres-test-container.ts` documents the equivalent interfaces and this file's own class comment states it "Mirrors `PostgresTestContainer`".

The new `BULLMQ_PREFIX` DI Symbol token was placed in a dedicated `bullmq-prefix.token.ts` file, while every other existing DI Symbol token in `apps/api/src` is co-located inside a broader-purpose file (a factory, interface, or constants file) — making this the first standalone token file and a precedent for future inconsistency.

The default `'bull'` BullMQ prefix was applied in the DI factory (`env.get('BULLMQ_PREFIX') ?? 'bull'`) instead of in the Zod schema, breaking from the project's established schema-default + `getOrThrow` pattern used elsewhere in `api.schema.ts`, risking the default drifting out of sync if only one of the two sites were ever updated.
